title: Isaiah, Chapter 4 (Great Isaiah Scroll, 1QIsa-a)
source: Great Isaiah Scroll 1QIsa-a: Israel Museum / Google Art Project photograph (Wikimedia Commons, PD) + ETCBC dss transcription (Abegg; CC BY-NC 4.0) + KJV (bible-api.com)
description: Isaiah 4 as written in the Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a, c. 125 BCE, Qumran Cave 1, Israel Museum), shown with the specific scroll column(s) 4 that carry each section. Hebrew is the scroll's own transcription (ETCBC dss / Abegg), not the Masoretic text; English is the King James Version.
introduction:
Isaiah 4 from the Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaa), the complete copy of Isaiah found in Cave 1 at Qumran in 1947 and now in the Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem. Copied around 125 BCE, it is roughly a thousand years older than the Leningrad Codex, the oldest complete Masoretic manuscript. This chapter stands in col. IV (4) of the scroll's 54 columns.

  1. Scan: each section is shown with the actual column of the scroll that carries it, cropped from the Israel Museum / Google Art Project photograph of the whole scroll published on Wikimedia Commons (public domain). The column for every verse comes from the transcription itself, which records the column and line of each word.
  2. Hebrew: the scroll's own text, verbatim from the ETCBC dss Text-Fabric dataset (Jacobs, Naaijer and Roorda, from Martin G. Abegg Jr.'s transcription; CC BY-NC 4.0). This is not the Masoretic text: 1QIsaa uses a fuller spelling (for example לוא for לא, כיא for כי) and differs from the Masoretic text in a number of readings. No vowel points exist in the scroll and none are added. Marks: ⟨x⟩ letters the scribe added above the line, [x] modern reconstruction of text lost to damage, {{x}} letters cancelled by an ancient scribe, ⟪x⟫ an ancient correction, a dot under a letter (x̣) an uncertain reading, ···· four dots written in place of the divine name (Tetrapuncta).
  3. English: the King James Version (1611, public domain), verbatim from bible-api.com. The KJV translates the Masoretic text, so where the scroll reads differently the English will not match the Hebrew shown; the scroll's reading can be checked on the column image.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>וה⟨ח⟩זיקה שבע נשים באיש אחד ביום ההוא לאמור לחמנו נאכל ושלמתנו נלבש רק יקרא שמך עלינו אסף חרפתנו <sup>2</sup>ביום ההוא יהיה צמח יהוה לצבי ולכבוד ופרי הארץ לגאון ולתפארת לפליטת ישראל ויהודה <sup>3</sup>ויהיה הנשאר בציון והנותר בירושלם קדוש יאמר לו כול הכתוב לחיים בירושלם <sup>4</sup>אמ רחץ אדוני את צאת בנות ציון ואת דמי ירושלם ידיח מקרבה ברוח משפט וברוח סער <sup>5</sup>ויברא יהוה על כול מכון הר ציון ועל מקראה ענן יוממ <sup>6</sup>מחרב ולמחסה ולמסתור מזרם וממטר
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>And in that day seven women shall take hold of one man, saying, We will eat our own bread, and wear our own apparel: only let us be called by thy name, to take away our reproach. <sup>2</sup>In that day shall the branch of the LORD be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the earth shall be excellent and comely for them that are escaped of Israel. <sup>3</sup>And it shall come to pass, that he that is left in Zion, and he that remaineth in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, even every one that is written among the living in Jerusalem: <sup>4</sup>When the Lord shall have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and shall have purged the blood of Jerusalem from the midst thereof by the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning. <sup>5</sup>And the LORD will create upon every dwelling place of mount Zion, and upon her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night: for upon all the glory shall be a defence. <sup>6</sup>And there shall be a tabernacle for a shadow in the daytime from the heat, and for a place of refuge, and for a covert from storm and from rain.
